questions.question: Which three annotations does @SpringBootApplication combine?
questions.explanation: It marks the main configuration class, switches on auto-configuration and scans the package for components.

questions.question: In an interview you are asked why constructor injection is preferred. Which answer is best?
options: It makes the app start faster than any other style
It is the only style Spring supports
It makes dependencies clear, allows final fields and works in tests without Spring
It removes the need for beans
questions.explanation: Constructor injection states the dependencies openly, keeps fields immutable and lets you build the object in a plain unit test.

questions.question: application.properties has server.port=8081. The JAR starts with the command-line option --server.port=9090. Which port does the app use?
questions.explanation: Command-line options have the highest priority among the common configuration sources.

questions.question: A @RestController method returns a List of records with a name and a price. What does the client receive?
options: The text of the list's toString() only
Nothing, because a return type is required to be String
questions.explanation: In a @RestController the return value goes through JSON conversion, so a list of records becomes a JSON array.

questions.question: A @Transactional method calls another @Transactional method of the same class using this. The second method's transaction settings are ignored. Why?
options: Transactions work only on private methods
The call skips the Spring proxy, so no transaction advice runs
The database does not allow nested calls
questions.explanation: Spring applies transactions through a proxy. A call from inside the same object does not pass through it.
